documents: Rusakov et al. 2022, Boreas 51, 859-876 (published paper, PDF; supplementary Tables S1-S5 referenced but not supplied)

entry.evidence: The main objective of this study was to obtain insights into the Holocene glaciation history of the eastern ice fields on Novaya Zemlya

steps.action: Frame the gap: fjord sediment histories exist only for the west coast (Russkaya Gavan', last 800 years), so the authors set out to reconstruct the Holocene glaciation history of the eastern ice fields.
steps.quote: The main objective of this study was to obtain insights into the Holocene glaciation history of the eastern ice fields on Novaya Zemlya

steps.action: Take from published work the west-east climate and precipitation gradient across the North Island and the moisture barrier for North Atlantic air flow.
steps.quote: A climate gradient exists across the North Island.

steps.action: Collect a box core and a 472 cm gravity core (AMK-5251) in the outer basin of Tsivol'ki Fjord in 2015; inner-basin sampling near the glacier front failed because of high water content.
steps.quote: attempts to collect bottom sediments in the inner basin close to the glacier front were unsuccessful

steps.action: Date benthic foraminifera and bulk organic carbon by AMS 14C and build a Bacon age-depth model from the foraminiferal dates (Marine20, 402-year reservoir correction), giving sedimentation rates.
steps.quote: The age model was created based on the results of dating the benthic foraminifera.

steps.action: Measure grain size (wet sieving and decantation), mineralogy (XRD with Rietveld quantification), major elements (XRF and ICP-AES) and planktic and benthic microfossils down the core.
steps.quote: The chemical composition was studied at the Laboratory of Matter Analysis at the GEOKhI by two methods

steps.action: Calibrate the XRF against 36 standard samples and cross-check element contents between XRF and ICP-AES (discrepancy within one standard deviation).
steps.quote: The discrepancy in determining the content of the chemical elements

steps.action: Describe the core lithology and mineralogy and divide it into three lithofacies (LF3 472-235 cm, LF2 235-25 cm, LF1 25-0 cm).
steps.quote: These sediments form separate layer packs

steps.action: Compare grain size, water content and chemistry of the box-core and gravity-core tops, find that the gravity corer destroyed the upper 7 cm, and correct the composite depth scale.
steps.quote: it was found that the gravity corer destroyed the upper 7 cm of the sediment

steps.action: Apply factor analysis to the grain-size, mineral and chemical data to find the dominant factors and associations by lithofacies; mineral associations are not repeated (non-cyclic).
steps.quote: identify the two most significant factors explaining, in total, 85.1% of the variations

steps.action: Compare bulk-organic and carbonate-shell 14C ages in the same core (a near-linear 12-15 ka offset) and infer that bulk organic carbon is mainly old glacier-delivered material.
steps.quote: the main source of the total organic carbon in the fjord sediments does not originate from in situ bioproduction

steps.action: Propose that young organic matter is diluted by older detrital carbon from several possible sources.
steps.quote: We hypothesize that young organic matter (from in situ bioproduction or production in river waters) is diluted with older material

steps.action: Compare the fjord's bulk organic ages with published ages of Ob', Yenisei and Lena river particulates to argue for a glacial signal.
steps.quote: the terrigenous total organic matter in the Holocene sediments of the fjord is much older than

steps.action: Interpret LF3 mineralogy, geochemistry and grain-size factors as proximal glaciomarine sediment from weakly altered archipelago rocks, with sub-sections of changing conditions.
steps.quote: reflecting the provenance of the archipelago’s weakly altered magmatic and metamorphic rocks

steps.action: Interpret LF2 and LF1: coarse-silt dominance, Mn enrichment as an aerated ice-free fjord, and LF1 clay content as distal glaciomarine sediment.
steps.quote: characteristic of distal glaciomarine sediments

steps.action: Check microfossils for carbonate dissolution and find no traces, even on thin planktic shells, to exclude a preservation artifact.
steps.quote: The effect of dissolution of biogenic carbonate can be excluded

steps.action: Show that the microfossil abundance and diversity zonation independently reproduces the three lithofacies.
steps.quote: core AMK-5251 can be divided also into three vertical sections, each of which reflects the lithofacies highlighted above

steps.action: Infer palaeoenvironments from foraminiferal ecology: high summer bioproduction and a proximal glacier front before c. 4.6 cal. ka BP, then meltwater-dominated turbid conditions.
steps.quote: a proximal position of the core site to the glacier front prior to c. 4.6 cal. ka BP

steps.action: Offer two explanations for the low microfossil content at 4.6-3.6 ka: suppressed photosynthetic plankton under suspended load, or dilution under high sedimentation rates.
steps.quote: Their low numbers could also be caused by sediment dilution under high sedimentation rates.

steps.action: Assemble the early-phase glacier history (10.6-4.6 ka): onset of glaciomarine sedimentation by 10.6 ka, severe sea ice, iceberg calving, then increased meltwater.
steps.quote: glaciomarine sedimentation in the outer part of the Tsivol’ki Fjord commenced already by

steps.action: Link middle-phase shallowing and weaker water exchange to glacio-isostatic uplift documented by published raised-beach and radiocarbon evidence.
steps.quote: The latter may have resulted from a shallowing of the fjord owing to the glacio-isostatic uplift of the North Island

steps.action: Propose, hypothetically, that the absence of intact bivalve shells after 6 ka reflects redeposition from the wave-breaking zone as the fjord shallowed.
steps.quote: Hypothetically, the absence of intact shells of bivalve molluscs

steps.action: Relate LF1 IRD peaks to the Medieval Climate Anomaly, the Little Ice Age and Modern Warming, and contrast them with the Russkaya Gavan' record.
steps.quote: can be explained by fluctuations in the tidewater glacier front

steps.action: Explain the absence of Neoglacial advances, unlike Svalbard, by dry continental air masses and the Siberian High blocking North Atlantic moisture.
steps.quote: may be explained by the atmospheric conditions over the east coast of Novaya Zemlya

steps.action: Conclude a three-phase Holocene history of the Serp-i-Molot glacier, with sub-events in each phase.
steps.quote: reveals three main phases in the Holocene history of the Serp-i-Molot tidewater glacier

tree.answer: Holocene history of an eastern Novaya Zemlya tidewater glacier, unstudied
No; inferred from fjord sediment traces
Reconstruct glacier and fjord phases through the Holocene
Only ad hoc local rivals (dilution vs suppressed production; climate explanation for no Neoglacial advance)
No distinct predictions derived for rivals
Conditions found: one core at one outer-basin site
Partly: proxies agree on zonation; analytical cross-check; no replicate core
Three-phase history kept as best explanation

end.claim: The Serp-i-Molot glacier front lay near the fjord mouth c. 10.6-4.6 cal. ka BP, retreated as the fjord shallowed by glacio-isostatic uplift c. 4.6-0.9 ka, and has been stable in the inner fjord since 0.9±0.1 ka, without major Neoglacial advances.

decisive_move.sentence: The multiproxy measurements on the single dated core AMK-5251 (grain size, XRD, XRF/ICP, microfossils), placed on the foraminiferal age model, supply every phase boundary; without them no history exists.

gates.evidence: Coring was driven by an objective (fill the eastern-coast gap), not by a stated hypothesis. The phases could have failed to agree across lithology, geochemistry and microfossils (they agree, p. 868), but no rival history was given a test. Nothing was fixed before the data.

imports.item: Bacon Bayesian age-depth modelling (autoregressive gamma process) in R
XRF and ICP atomic emission spectrometry
Stokes law for settling in grain-size decantation

novelty_claims.quote: For the first time, the Holocene history of the Serp-i-Molot tidewater glacier at the eastern side of the Novaya Zemlya archipelago, Kara Sea, has been [...]

limits: Claim rests on one core from one outer-basin site; the inner basin could not be sampled. The age model rests on four foraminiferal dates over 472 cm and uses the standard 402-year reservoir correction without a local ΔR (inference: phase-boundary ages carry unstated uncertainty beyond the few ± values given). LF1 has a single date, so links to the Medieval Climate Anomaly, Little Ice Age and Modern Warming are not resolved chronologically (sub-claim: best_explanation, weak). The text calls LF1 both a glacier-front stabilization and the most active frontal retreat, an internal tension. The Neoglacial-absence explanation (Siberian High, dry continental air) is argued from cited climatology, not tested (sub-claim: best_explanation, untested). Glacio-isostatic shallowing is inferred from cited uplift data (best_explanation). Supplementary Tables S1-S5 were not supplied, so values cited from them could not be checked. No review file was supplied. Whether the analyses were planned before the cruise is not stated.
